factual_basis_before: GreyNoise's primary threat-intelligence disclosure states that it directly observed the campaign through its Global Observation Grid, traced orchestration to malicious infrastructure it had followed since July 2026, and observed the actor build a PaperCut and Active Directory lab, generate target lists, then deploy hundreds of AI agents against real systems. GreyNoise attributes the agent stack to OpenAI's Codex harness and a DeepSeek model, explicitly distinguishing the DeepSeek model from OpenAI models. It reports at least 440 compromised instances at 395 identified organizations in 48 countries, credential harvesting across many victims, domain-administrator access at 12 organizations, and full NTDS.DIT credential-database exfiltration where domain admin was obtained. PaperCut's own security bulletin independently confirms active exploitation and customer incidents involving CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078. OECD.AI indexes the campaign as an AI incident but is retained only as secondary registry evidence. The dated timeline places initial real-target exploitation before the wider campaign, with later follow-up varying by victim. One specific WAF block is documented. PaperCut’s September 10 update explicitly says it had not independently verified GreyNoise’s indicators; its customer reports corroborate exploitation of the vulnerabilities, not every detail or victim of this campaign. Patch publication and coordinated notifications do not establish fleet-wide recovery.
